observations.openingColdNotes: Played cold at 390x844 in Playwright Chromium with hasTouch/isMobile, before reading NOTES.md or source. Title screen has a drowned-city skyline, lanterns and a clear 'Cast off'. The intro states the debt (¤6,000 to Marrow Quill at 6% a night, due night 10), the ¤2,500 purse and the 30-night goal. The 5-step tour covers the ledger, first trade, canals, harbor services and the deadline. Night 1 shows a 'harbor circular' with all ports' quotes and a top banner: 'Compare 13 Bottled Rain → Saint Mire, ¤291, 1 night, risk 2/5, possible Gull toll ¤283, at 20% lower +¤972'. The trade sheet preselects a reserve-keeping quantity (13 of a possible 15) and states 'leak patch ¤234 / Gull toll ¤283, your remaining purse covers either bill'. I understood the first buy, the voyage and the sale without help. Early confusion: tapping the banner opened the map route rather than the trade sheet. I found the fleet calendar (wireless icon) only on night 9.
observations.1_trade_and_cargo: Run 1, hand-played by touch, decisions with runner-ups. N1: Bottled Rain x13 at default reserve; runner-ups were Max x15 or Rust Pearls x6 to the Exchange (+¤144). N2: 3 Synth Saffron + 27 Glowkelp to Lanternquay; runner-up was 4 saffron + 26 kelp to Fogmouth; the sheet showed the purse ¤196 short of the bill when I pushed quantity. N6: 4 eels (¤6,976) rather than ¤2,500 racks, because cash, not hold, was binding. N12: sold 3 saffron at ¤899 rather than carry them to the Fogmouth fleet at danger 4/5. The runner-up would have won: saffron hit ¤1,916 there on N14. N20: 1 Dreamsilk + harbor post to the Orchid fleet; runner-up was racks for bonded freight. N22: 1 silk + ¤5k vault, keeping ¤6.1k ≥ the ¤5,880 patch; runner-up 2 silks with no patch reserve. N27: 2 Moon Ink + only 2 chips so the purse kept ¤14.9k ≥ the ¤11.4k ink patch; runner-up 5 chips. Closing N29: 9 eels at default depth to Lanternquay for night-30 settlement (the Exchange eel fleet was 2 nights away, too late). Price impact is explicit: rain default 38 vs Max 45 at '¤117 avg, last at ¤101'; saffron Max 35 at '¤1,796 avg, last at ¤4,015'. A changed constraint flips the choice: in run 2 N1 I used Max (¤76 left, sheet warned '¤392 short'), and a leak forced jettisoning 6 rain I could not patch for ¤468. Strongest counterevidence: high-ticket goods (silk, ink) cap at 1–2 units, which makes composition trivial on those turns. Because tolls scale with the purse, depositing in the vault becomes a near-automatic step.
observations.2_routes_and_market_intelligence: Real spatial map: Lanternquay hub plus a 6-port ring. Route cards show nights, risk x/5, toll in cash, quote age and a 'test a price N% lower' scenario. Port details list usual supplies and imports and dated quotes for the hold. I compared competing routes on timing and risk: N4 Fogmouth→Lanternquay (1n-old quotes, risk 1) against Copperhook (4n old, risk 2). On N16, Lanternquay chips at ¤4,684 (1n old, risk 1) against the Exchange at ¤5,945 (6n old, risk 2); I took the Exchange and sold at ¤4,566. N25 bonded freight: direct 2n via Lanternquay against stopping at Lanternquay to trade. Quote vs arrival observations, all before any information upgrade: rain 291→245 (−16%), saffron 1,488→1,075 (−28%, beyond the 25% scenario), eels 3,335→2,899 (−13%), chips 5,783→4,905 (−15%), silk 9,970→6,465, rain 223→144 (−35%), ink 30,455→21,342 (−30%). Two arrivals had no buyer at all: saffron at Fogmouth N4 (dock factor at 60%) and eels at Lanternquay N9; both route cards had warned 'Buyer may be absent'. The fleet calendar is a reliable forward signal, and the N8 rumour stated its odds ('lands in full about half the time') and landed. Gap: I never bought the ¤6,000 wireless, so I have no after-upgrade comparison, which the 90 anchor requires. Counterevidence: realised drops often exceeded the offered lower-price scenario. Sparkline trends are readable, but the age-based reliability is only qualitative.
observations.3_economy_and_progression: Debt, borrow-against-net-worth, vault, racks, engine, weapons, wireless, charters, whispers, harbor post, and bonded and heavy freight all work and compete for funds. Run 1: repaid the full debt N7, then borrowed ¤3,600 to double a chip buy (+¤1,992 against ¤216 interest). Run 2: bought racks at N6 for capacity-capped loops, borrowed ¤4,000 at N7 for a fleet saffron loop and repaid before N10. Run 1 late game: racks from an event (¤4,720) unlocked bonded freight (¤18k stake → ¤42k by N28, delivered N27). That is two investment approaches with useful later options. Scripted default-strategy check (labeled scratch bot, seeded, follows the top banner at default quantity): repay-first on N1 starved trading and stalled at net worth −¤3.0k on N10. A banner bot that repays from N6 reached −¤4.5k on seed 101 and +¤6.3k on seed 202. My fleet-aware hand run 2 reached ¤18.2k debt-free, and hand run 1 ¤6.7k with ¤4.3k overdue. Suspected shortcut: bonded freight. It needs 45 hold, 40 free slots, an ¤18k stake at risk of seizure and a 1–2 night trip to danger-4 Fogmouth. Its +¤24k was comparable to 2 nights of my ~¤30k-capital trading then, so it is not a bypass. I did not run a matched-state freight-vs-trade fixture. Counterevidence: charters (¤20k) showed '+¤0 for this load' and never tempted me. Wireless at ¤6,000 was ~85% of my N17 net worth, so I never bought it. Because tolls scale with the purse, vault deposits are an obvious default. My ¤101k against the frozen keyboard runner's ¤340k shows depth, but my run used only part of the upgrade tree.
observations.4_risk_consequences_recovery: Offers disclose odds and ranges, and outcomes matched them. Tidewarden N3 'Run 44%, fail 7–14% hull': two fails at −8% and −8%, then the 'guaranteed' ¤720 bribe charged exactly ¤720. Gull Gang N8 'run 37%, fail 9–18%': −16% and −14%, then a toll of '¤589 + 1 eel' taken exactly. N14 fight '25%/volley, win ¤510–¤1,360': one miss at −9% (within 12%), then a win of ¤1,304 and 3 quieter nights. Collectors: 1 saffron for ¤825 off the debt, as quoted. The N23 Gull toll of ¤4,473 equalled the trade sheet's 'Gull toll demands ¤4,473'. Leak N11: the patch cost ¤5,880 the sheet had quoted at purchase. I could not afford it and lost a ¤6,389 Dreamsilk. Material hit and recovery: on N11 I had net worth ¤1.3k, ¤0 purse and overdue 10% debt. I recovered by partial repayment, paying collectors in kind, a full hull repair, a cheap pearls run, the Fogmouth fleet, the harbor post and a won fight. Debt was clear by N15 and net worth was ¤16k by N20. Counterevidence: 'risk about 12% of each cargo' never triggered in four failed runs; this is plausible but unverified. Grandmother Wick's gamble is EV-neutral (40% × 2.5) and appeared three times. Hull repair applied the whole ¤1,610 with one tap and no amount choice.
observations.5_run_pacing_and_ending: Each phase played differently. Opening (N1–10): the debt clock and a 6% hurdle shaped the deadline choices. Middle (N11–20): recovery, fleet calls, the harbor post from N15 and the racks offer. Closing (N21–30): bonded and heavy freight, deposits sized against purse-scaled tolls, and the N28–29 choice to sell ink at a certain ¤21.3k rather than gamble 2-night-old Sluices quotes. N30 shows 'Final night · settle for ¤X', a half-value dump warning and a confirmation. No stretch of more than two nights lacked a meaningful choice: every port night offered a buy/sell/route decision, and events interleaved. Ending: rank 'Canal Runner', ¤148,440 short of Lantern Broker. Cash ¤29,371 + vault ¤72,189 = ¤101,560, which reconciles exactly, with voyages, best profit, peak worth, encounters, debt interest and vault interest. Counterevidence: the 'Losses and forfeits ¤17.3k' total is not itemised. My own tally of bribes, tolls, the jettisoned silk and collector cargo comes to ≈¤18k, so I could not reconcile that line exactly.
observations.6_replay_and_adaptation: Run 2 (fresh, through N10; FAST acceleration on, visible touch controls, my choices): the fleet calendar's first two calls matched run 1's neighbourhood, but N13+ differed: Glowkelp→Copperhook, chips→Sluices N17, saffron→Lanternquay N21, eels→Exchange N25, silk→Orchid N29. Early adaptation: I read the calendar on N1, looped rain twice through the Saint Mire fleet, then took saffron to the Fogmouth fleet and caught a surge at ¤2,773. Later adaptation: racks on N6 for capacity, borrowing ¤4k after a full repay and clearing it by N9, and a 1-silk/2-silk choice sized to the ¤5,880 patch. N10 result: ¤18.2k debt-free, against run 1's ¤6.7k with overdue debt. Approaches I would try next: wireless early to avoid the absent-buyer losses; Ysolde whispers (¤570) against surge rumours; heavy freight (65 hold, ¤50k stake). Counterevidence: both hand runs opened with the same banner (rain → Saint Mire), so the very first move did not change. The scripted bot seeds opened with saffron → Fogmouth instead.
observations.7_onboarding_and_decision_clarity: On-screen cues explained each step. First buy: the default quantity with a 15% reserve and its stated rationale. First voyage: the route card's nights, risk and toll. First sale: profit against average cost. An unexpected price: arrival drops were pre-flagged with 'Buyer may be absent. Test 25% lower', and the dock factor explained a 60% offer. Relevant constraints: '¤196 short of the larger bill', 'Not enough cash aboard for the patch', HOLD 30/30, and the 'Explain debt' HUD tap stating 10% after night 10 plus collectors. After night 3 I made independent choices without looking up rules. Counterevidence: the tour says the debt 'must be repaid by night 10', but the actual rule (rate rises, collectors) appears only under the HUD explainer. The 'leak patch costs ¤3,120' line for a single chip was puzzling until a leak happened. The fleet calendar sits behind an unlabeled radio icon, and I discovered it on N9. Tapping a route banner opens the map rather than the trade sheet. The repair button acted without confirmation.
observations.8_input_and_accessibility: Touch (emulated) reached settlement at 390x844 in my run 1 (29 voyages, visible controls only). Every visible control on the market, map, map-with-selection, harbor and menu measured at least 44 px; trade-sheet controls measured 46–52 px. At 1280x800 my own checks covered: keyboard start (Tab/Enter), arrow-key good selection, B to buy, Tab to 'Buy 16', Enter, and focus returning to the row. Keys 2/3 selected a district with focus on 'Sail here · 1 night', Enter sailed. The squall event opened with focus on option 1 and a gold focus ring, and key '2' chose Shelter. A mouse click on the row Sell button and the confirm worked. Settlement by keyboard comes from the frozen keyboard-play.cjs runner (scripted, native keys, 0 pointer events, reached the ending and ledger). Text contrast: an approximate computed-colour check found every visible text node at least 4.5:1, except the gradient-filled title (false positive). A prefers-reduced-motion media rule exists. Non-colour cues: 'Cheap/Pricey/Surge' tags, ±% text, and risk shown both as pips and as 'risk 2/5'. Defect: the How-to-play Controls table at 1280 renders key chips misaligned across grid cells ('1 –', '7 Pick a district', '↑'/'↓' detached), making the keyboard legend hard to read.
observations.9_world_feedback_sound: Seven illustrated districts (lighthouse Fogmouth, crane Copperhook, pump-wheel Sluices, bank-columned Exchange, lantern hub) with short lore lines and named characters: Marrow Quill, Pell the lamplighter, Grandmother Wick, Madame Ysolde, Old Fenna. Actions read without the log: buy/sell notices ('Loaded 13 Bottled Rain for ¤2,054') with purse ± deltas flashed on the HUD; a voyage animation along a dashed canal; event cards with their own art (searchlights, lightning squall); a victory card; an ending card with a crest. Sound operation, instrumented rather than heard: new oscillator/buffer sources per action were buy +2/+1, sell +3/+1 and sail +8/+2. Pressing M stopped all new nodes during a sell, and the aria-pressed state toggled. Pace: voyages take ~3 s at normal speed, with a tap-to-skip available. Counterevidence: Grandmother Wick repeated three times in one run. Event art reuses a few templates. I could not judge listening quality.
observations.10_reliability_and_delivery: One 272,410-byte self-contained game/index.html (under 1 MB). The only URL in the source is the SVG namespace. NOTES.md has 59 lines. Across my touch run, run 2, the desktop session, and the denied-storage, corrupt-storage and sandbox checks: zero page errors and zero non-file requests. The score survived a reload in the Captains' Ledger. Denied localStorage (a throwing getter) still played. Corrupting all three real keys showed 'Your saved voyage could not be loaded. Start a new run.' with an empty ledger and no errors. A sandbox iframe without allow-same-origin booted and started a voyage. Arithmetic checks: the ending reconciled cash + vault = final fortune; the trade-sheet totals matched purse changes (e.g., 16 × ¤123 = ¤1,968); repay and borrow previews matched their results. Frozen helpers with scratch output all passed: verify.cjs (8/8, including WebKit touch at 4 sizes, desktop, two full games, corrupt storage and sandbox), event-check (16/16), trading-check (pass), pr-check (30/30) and keyboard-play (full game, ¤340,145, reload ledger). Defects found are noncritical UX (repair has no confirm; help table layout).

priorities: Make market-signal reliability quantitative and give the information upgrade a real place. Realised arrival prices often fell beyond the offered '25% lower' scenario (−28%, −30%, −35%), and two arrivals had no buyer at all. Show an age-based expected spread or a buyer-presence chance on route cards. Also reconsider a ¤6,000 all-or-nothing wireless, which a mid-run player cannot justify (for example, a cheaper single-port wire or a price that scales).

Surface the fleet calendar where plans are made: a strip on the market or map, not only behind the unlabeled radio icon. Explain its effect in the tour. It was the strongest planning tool and I found it only on night 9; using it from night 1 in run 2 nearly tripled my night-10 worth.

Tighten the finance and feedback edges. Hull repair should ask for an amount and a confirmation (one tap spent ¤1,610). The ending should itemise 'Losses and forfeits'. Rotate or retire repeated EV-neutral events (Grandmother Wick appeared 3 times). Fix the desktop How-to-play Controls table layout.
limits: Touch was Playwright Chromium emulation (hasTouch/isMobile, 390x844, DSF 2), not a physical phone: no real gestures, safe-area, rubber-banding or silent-switch behaviour.
Audio was not heard. Sound-cue operation and mute were verified by instrumenting AudioContext.createOscillator/createBufferSource counts per action, so listening quality is unjudged.

One full hand-played run to settlement (run 1, no acceleration, touch). Run 2 was hand-played to night 10 with the game's FAST flag on. Desktop checks covered trade, route and event personally; keyboard settlement relies on the frozen keyboard-play.cjs runner.

Scripted evidence, explicitly labeled: the scratch 'banner-follow default' bot (seeds 101 and 202, nights 1–10, all choices made by script), the frozen helpers verify.cjs, event-check.cjs, trading-check.cjs, pr-check.cjs and keyboard-play.cjs (scratch output only), and touch-play.cjs (390x844 emulated touch, seed 31: passed, reached night 30 and a Lantern Broker settlement with no errors or network requests).

Contrast was checked by computed foreground against the nearest opaque ancestor background, so translucent layers and gradients are approximated; it was a single-screen sample at 1280 plus visual review at 390.

Not exercised personally: the wireless set, whispers, engine, weapons, charters and heavy freight. No matched-state fixture compared bonded freight against trading. The economy criterion relies on my two runs, the default-bot comparison and the notes' bot claims, which I treated as unverified context.

The run-1 decision log was reconstructed from the game's on-screen quotes recorded during play; the runner-up outcomes are counterfactual estimates except where later prices revealed them (N12 saffron, N8 pearls in run 2).
